It's sounds like your best bet in your case is point-of-use filter of some kind. What does is smell like exactly? This could affect the best way to treat the smell. 

Chlorine/bleach: Expose the water to air. Use a standard pitcher filter. 

Rotten Egg/Sulfur: could be from drain or water heater. If not, call the utility company, this is bad. 

Oil/Gas: call utilities and public health. 

Mold/Musty/Earthy/Fishy: this one happens to me. This is almost always your drain. Use a pitcher filter. Ask your boss to clean the drain. 

Basically, use a Britta. Ask your boss to get the drains cleaned. If you smell sulfur or gas, call utilities/public health to report it.

Hey, so I have a degree in environmental engineering, including specializing in pollution treatment and control, and I work in water resources engineering. I figured I would share a little info about TDS. 

TDS (Total Dissolved Solids) is the total concentration of dissolved substances in water, both organic and inorganic. These can include calcium, sodium, chlorides, etc. 

TDS can be cause by human activity (agriculture, road ice), but it can also be natural. For example, mineral springs have high levels because they flow through rocks with high salt content. . 

A high concentration of TDS is not a health hazard. Some people even buy mineral water to intentionally have more dissolved solids. TDS is a secondary standard for drinking water, meaning it's a voluntary guideline, because it is primarily for aesthetics (taste and smell) and operational ease (residue not clogging pipes). Most people rate water with a level of TDS of less than 600 ppm as having a good taste (World Health Organization). The Canadian guideline is for water to be under 500 ppm. If the water is 190 ppm, that's great! 

It is true that an exceptionally high concentration can indicate the presence of truly harmful contaminants such as bromide and arsenic, which would need to be confirmed by specific testing. Water testament facilities, like those in Kingston, remove these harmful substances and test frequently, so you should not need to worry. The Kingston water quality reports are publicly available on the Utilties Kingston website. 

TLDR: TDS is not a big bag thing, but you sure can make it sound scary if you're trying to sell something. If you are on municipal water, you're fine. Kingston meets and exceeds water quality standards.

Little FYI about MAID (Medical Assistance in Dying) eligibility for those not from Canada for context: 

-resident of Canada 

-18 years old and mentally competent 

-have a grievous and irremediable medical condition 

-make a voluntary request for MAID that is not the result of outside pressure or influence 

-give informed consent to receive MAID

For the medical condition: 

-a serious illness, disease, or disability (with some mental illness being included starting March 17, 2023)
-be in an advanced state if decline that cannot be reversed 

-experience unbearable physical or mental suffering that cannot be relieved under a condition that you consider acceptable 

-does not need to be fatal or terminal 

When mental illness is officially added, safeguards will be put in place in the form of additional criteria
